mission_1.search:
BFS path length 13.5 m with 923 expanded nodes. A* path length 13.5 m with 700 expanded nodes. The lengths are equal, and A* looked at 223 fewer cells.

In my bfs(), the frontier is a deque and I always popleft() the oldest cell, so cells are expanded in rings of increasing distance from the start in every direction, including directions that lead away from the goal. BFS only stops when the goal is discovered, so it has to finish almost every ring closer than the goal first.

In my astar(), the frontier is a heap ordered by f = g + ctx.heuristic(cell), where g is the number of moves so far (best_g) and h is the Manhattan distance to the goal. Cells that move away from the goal get a larger f and stay lower in the heap, so many of them are never popped before the goal is. Manhattan distance never overestimates on this 4-connected unit-cost grid, so when the goal is removed from the heap its g is already the cheapest, which is why A* returns the same 13.5 m route as BFS. The heuristic changes the order of examination, not the route length.
mission_1.failure:
On the constrained map, BFS succeeded with 24.5 m, 843 expansions, peak frontier 14. DFS succeeded with 50.0 m, 448 expansions, peak frontier 200. IDDFS stopped with resource_limit after 250,001 expansions and returned no route.

One difference in path length is that dfs() keeps following one branch at a time. In my implementation, it always takes the right first, because I push neighbours in reverse so the first supplied neighbour is on top. A cell is marked as a parent when it is first pushed and never improved, so the route is simply the first branch that reaches the goal, about twice the shortest. It used fewer expansions than BFS because it stopped as soon as that branch hit the goal, but its frontier was larger because every cell on the deep branch leaves its other neighbours waiting on the stack.

In the unreachable case. BFS no_path (9 expansions), DFS no_path (9), IDDFS no_path (231), A* no_path (9). no_path means the search finished: the queue, stack or heap became empty (for IDDFS, a whole pass finished with no depth cutoff), so every reachable cell was tried, and no route exists. resource_limit means the runner stopped an unfinished search when ctx.expand raised its budget exception. It says nothing about whether a path exists.

I used Claude to explain how to fix bugs in all four algorithm implementation drafts. I checked the results with the six checks and the full evaluation table, confirmed BFS and A* match the shortest length, and confirmed the unreachable case returns no_path for all four.
